definitions.standard: The splitting of white light into its component colors.
definitions.simple: When white light breaks apart into a beautiful rainbow of seven different colors.
definitions.scientific: The separation of white light into colors, or of any radiation according to wavelength, typically caused by a prism or grating.

linguistics.origin: From Latin 'dispersio', meaning 'scattering or breaking apart'.

examples: Colors seen on a soap bubble
Colors reflecting off the back of a CD
counter_examples: A red laser beam going through a prism (it stays red)
Painting a wall with mixed colors
real_world_applications: Spectroscopy to find what stars are made of

advanced_data.history: Sir Isaac Newton used a glass prism to demonstrate that white light is composed of the seven colors of the visible spectrum.

common_misconceptions: A prism magically adds color to white light. (Fact: The color is already inside the white light; the prism just separates it.)
tutor_context.tutor_hint: Ask the student: 'If you shine a pure red light through a prism, will it make a rainbow? Why or why not?'
